title: Implement live X Y transfer curve scope with moving dot and morphing crossfade
description:
Create Source/UI/TransferCurveScope.h and Source/UI/TransferCurveScope.cpp. Implement a juce::Component subclass named TransferCurveScope that renders a live X-Y transfer curve plot y = f(v) across the input amplitude domain, plus a moving dot indicating the instantaneous input amplitude, and a smooth morphing crossfade of the curve during voicing-mode changes. The component is a Timer-driven repaint consumer only: it reads instantaneous input amplitude and the current/target transfer-curve state through atomic values or a lock-free FIFO snapshot that the processor exposes. It must NEVER lock, block, or call the audio thread; the GUI only reads atomic telemetry. Provide a public API (e.g. setCurvePoints/pushInputSample or a snapshot-pull method) so PluginEditor can feed it telemetry, but do not include PluginProcessor here — depend only on plain atomics/parameters passed in.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/PluginEditor.h (namespace/class naming, how editor holds references)
- Source/PluginProcessor.h (what atomic telemetry / lock-free FIFO the DSP chain already exposes for the transfer curve and instantaneous amplitude; read only)
- JUCE/modules/juce_gui_basics/components/juce_Component.h and juce_events Timer API (do not modify anything under JUCE/)
acceptance_criteria: Source/UI/TransferCurveScope.h and Source/UI/TransferCurveScope.cpp exist and declare/define class TransferCurveScope deriving from juce::Component
TransferCurveScope renders a transfer curve, a moving input-amplitude dot, and crossfades between voicing curves in paint()
TransferCurveScope reads telemetry only through atomics or a lock-free snapshot and never locks or calls the audio thread
cmake --build build --target ShredBoost_VST3 succeeds after adding these files to the target sources
No file outside this task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify CMakeLists.txt (g.5 owns the CMake integration)
lock, block, or call the audio thread from GUI code
